step: Employment Pass Application via myMOM Portal
deadline_label: At least 3–8 weeks before intended start date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employer submits EP application via myMOM portal; MOM targets 3-week processing for straightforward online applications.
non_obvious_actual_reality: COMPASS points-based framework (mandatory 1 Sep 2023) means applications that cleared the old salary test may now fail on diversity or local workforce support criteria. Additional document requests extend processing to 8+ weeks. MOM may request a face-to-face meeting with the applicant.
non_obvious_action_required: Run MOM's COMPASS self-assessment calculator before submitting. Prepare educational certificates, payslips, and company ACRA business profile upfront. Flag borderline COMPASS scores to HR legal counsel — a refusal triggers a 3-month cooling-off period before reapplication.
source: MOM — Employment Pass: Apply for a Pass

step: COMPASS Points-Based Assessment
deadline_label: Before EP application submission
non_obvious_official_guidance: EP applicants assessed on four foundational criteria (salary benchmark, qualifications, diversity, local employment support) plus two bonus criteria (skills bonus, strategic economic priorities). Minimum 40 points required to pass.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The salary criterion scores against MOM's sector-specific percentile benchmarks — not simply the minimum threshold. An employee earning SGD 5,600 in tech may score only 10/20 if the sector median is SGD 8,000. The diversity criterion gives 20 points only if the applicant's nationality represents <5% of the firm's PMETs — a metric many SMEs have never tracked.
non_obvious_action_required: Download MOM's COMPASS framework document and run the full 6-criterion calculation before applying. If borderline, assess whether the Skills Bonus (20 points) from a pre-approved skills attestation body is achievable. Nationality headcount by PMET tier is rarely in HR systems — collate it before the application window.

step: EP Salary Threshold Verification
field_label: Fixed Monthly Salary vs MOM Threshold
deadline_label: Before application submission
non_obvious_official_guidance: Minimum fixed monthly salary for new EP applicants: SGD 5,600 (general); SGD 6,200 (financial services sector) from 1 January 2025. Older or more experienced candidates must earn higher — MOM benchmarks increase with age.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The stated minimums are floor thresholds, not approval guarantees. MOM's age-adjusted salary benchmarks mean a 45-year-old applicant earning SGD 7,000 may still score poorly on the salary criterion if the sector benchmark for that age band is SGD 12,000. Variable pay (bonus, commissions) does NOT count toward the salary threshold — only fixed monthly salary.
non_obvious_action_required: Obtain MOM's sector-specific salary benchmark data for the applicant's age band before setting the offer letter salary. If total compensation is competitive but fixed base is low, consider restructuring the fixed/variable split to clear the threshold.
source: MOM — EP Eligibility and Salary Requirements

step: S Pass Application and Quota Check
field_label: S Pass Application + Sector Quota Headroom
deadline_label: Before employee travels to Singapore
non_obvious_official_guidance: S Pass minimum salary: SGD 3,150/month (from 1 Sep 2023), rising to SGD 3,300/month from 1 Sep 2025. Subject to sector quota: 10% of workforce (services sector) or 15% (other sectors).
non_obvious_actual_reality: S Pass quota is calculated against total workforce headcount. An employer at 9.5% quota utilisation in the services sector has essentially no headroom — a new hire application will be refused regardless of individual eligibility. Quota data in myMOM is updated with a lag; employers near the ceiling have been surprised by refusals after investing months in recruitment.
non_obvious_action_required: Log in to myMOM to check current quota utilisation BEFORE making a job offer to an S Pass-category candidate. If at or near ceiling, a new S Pass approval requires either a local hire first or a headcount reduction elsewhere. Do not send IPA to employee until quota is confirmed available.

step: Work Permit Application — Source Country and Sector Eligibility
deadline_label: Before employee travels
non_obvious_official_guidance: Work Permits for semi-skilled workers: source country eligibility differs by sector (construction, marine, process, manufacturing, services). Employers must pay Foreign Worker Levy monthly.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Source country restrictions are sector-specific and change periodically — a national from a permitted country for construction may be prohibited in the services sector. WP holders from India and Sri Lanka were restricted from the services sector for a period. Employers often discover the restriction only at the application stage after the worker has resigned from their home-country job.
non_obvious_action_required: Verify source country eligibility for the specific sector using MOM's worker eligibility checker before recruiting. Include sector eligibility as a pre-offer screening step in the hiring workflow.
source: MOM — Work Permit for Foreign Workers

step: In-Principle Approval (IPA) Letter
field_label: IPA Letter Validity and Entry Instruction
deadline_label: IPA valid 6 months from issue (EP); employee must enter before expiry
responsible_party: Employer — must forward IPA to employee
non_obvious_official_guidance: MOM issues an IPA letter after approving the pass application. The employee must enter Singapore within the IPA validity period. For EP/S Pass: 6 months. For WP: typically 1 month.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The IPA is NOT the work pass — it is a single-journey entry authorisation. The employee enters on a Single Journey Visa endorsed on the IPA, not on the work pass itself. The actual pass card (EP card with FIN) is only issued after the pass issuance appointment in Singapore. If the employee enters, then exits and re-enters before the pass card is collected, they may need a re-entry permit.
non_obvious_action_required: Forward IPA to employee immediately upon receipt. Confirm employee enters Singapore within IPA validity. Book pass issuance appointment before travel so it can be completed promptly after arrival. Advise employee not to exit Singapore before collecting the physical pass card.

step: Dependant's Pass Application — EP Holder Family
field_label: Dependant's Pass for Spouse and Unmarried Children Under 21
deadline_label: Can be submitted concurrently with EP application
responsible_party: Employer (applying on behalf of EP holder)
non_obvious_official_guidance: EP holders earning ≥ SGD 6,000/month may apply for a Dependant's Pass (DP) for their spouse and unmarried children under 21. S Pass holders are not eligible to sponsor DPs.
non_obvious_actual_reality: S Pass holders have zero DP eligibility — a critical relocation planning point that determines whether the whole family move is viable. DP holders cannot work in Singapore on the DP alone; they require a separate Letter of Consent (LOC) or Employment Pass. DP approval is discretionary even if the EP holder meets the salary threshold — MOM assesses the application holistically.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm pass type (EP vs S Pass) determines dependant eligibility before the employee accepts an offer involving family relocation. If EP salary is between SGD 5,600 and SGD 5,999, DP is not available — adjust offer if family relocation is a condition of acceptance. Apply for DP concurrently with EP to minimise family separation.

step: Pass Issuance Appointment and FIN Issuance
field_label: Foreign Identification Number (FIN) on Pass Card
deadline_label: Within first week of arrival; before IPA single-journey visa expires
responsible_party: Employee (attended in person); Employer books appointment
non_obvious_official_guidance: EP/S Pass holders must attend a pass issuance appointment at MOM or collect from an authorised agent. The pass card bears the FIN (Foreign Identification Number), a unique 9-character identifier.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The FIN is the employee's master identifier for ALL downstream processes in Singapore: IRAS tax filing, CPF registration, bank account opening, SingPass, tenancy agreements, healthcare, and government services. Without the FIN, no bank account can be opened, no SingPass registered, no tax return filed. EP card collection can take 4–5 working days after the appointment if additional checks are triggered — delays cascade across onboarding.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the pass issuance appointment via myMOM BEFORE the employee travels so it can be completed in the first 1–2 business days after arrival. Treat FIN collection as Day-1 priority. Include FIN in onboarding data capture immediately — do not wait until Week 2 payroll setup.

step: Medical Examination at MOM-Approved Clinic (WP/S Pass)
applies_to_employee_types: S Pass holder (from specified source countries)
field_label: Medical Clearance — TB and HIV Screening
deadline_label: Within 2 weeks of arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: WP holders and S Pass holders from specified source countries must undergo a medical examination at an MOM-approved clinic within 2 weeks of arrival. Examination screens for tuberculosis and HIV.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Positive TB results trigger mandatory treatment under the Infectious Diseases Act and may result in pass cancellation. MOM-approved clinics are in high demand and often have 2–3 week waiting lists — booking on Day 1 of arrival is essential. Many first-time Singapore employers assume pass issuance equals medical clearance; it does not. The clinic submits results directly to MOM electronically.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the MOM-approved clinic appointment before or on the employee's first day in Singapore — do not wait until Week 2. Confirm the specific clinic is on MOM's approved list. Notify HR when clearance is confirmed; do not deploy WP holder to client sites until medical clearance is obtained.
source: MOM — Medical Examination for Foreign Workers

step: SingPass Digital Identity Registration
deadline_label: As soon as FIN is issued — within first week
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign work pass holders with a Singapore FIN can register for SingPass — Singapore's national digital identity system — using the SingPass mobile app and face verification.
non_obvious_actual_reality: SingPass is the gatekeeping credential for virtually every Singapore government e-service: IRAS myTax Portal, CPF Online, myMOM portal for address updates, MediShield Life, and HDB applications. Without SingPass, the employee cannot file taxes independently, cannot check their own pass status, and cannot access healthcare entitlements digitally. Face verification failures (poor lighting, changed appearance) require a trip to a SingPass counter and can take 1–2 weeks to resolve.
non_obvious_action_required: Include SingPass registration as a Day-1 onboarding task the moment FIN is in hand. Brief employee on face verification requirements (neutral expression, good lighting, no glasses). If face verification fails, guide employee to nearest SingPass counter immediately — do not let it drift as downstream services become blocked.

step: Employer Notification to MOM of Employee Commencement
deadline_label: Within 3 days of employment commencement
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employer must notify MOM when the pass holder commences employment via the myMOM portal.
source: MOM — After the Pass is Issued

step: Notification of Residential Address to MOM
deadline_label: Within 3 months of pass issuance (target within 2 weeks)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Pass holders must update their Singapore residential address with MOM within 3 months of the pass being issued. Update is made via myMOM portal using SingPass login.
non_obvious_actual_reality: MOM uses the registered address for levy notices, renewal reminders, and pass condition correspondence — failure to update means critical communications go to a wrong address and the employee remains in breach of a pass condition. Many first-time Singapore employees assume address registration is a formality handled by HR; MOM requires the employee to update it personally via SingPass.
non_obvious_action_required: Add residential address update to the first-month onboarding checklist. HR should verify via myMOM that the update has been completed before the 3-month deadline. If employee is in serviced accommodation initially, update again when permanent address is secured — do not leave it at the serviced apartment address indefinitely.

step: Stamp Duty on Tenancy Agreement
form_name: IRAS e-Stamping Portal — Stamp Duty Submission
deadline_label: Within 14 days of signing (if signed in Singapore); 30 days if signed overseas
non_obvious_official_guidance: Tenancy agreements must be stamped via IRAS e-Stamping portal. Rate: 0.4% of total rent for leases ≤4 years; 0.4% of 4× the average annual rent for leases >4 years. Minimum duty: SGD 1.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Unstamped tenancy agreements are inadmissible as evidence in Singapore courts — effectively unenforceable in a dispute. Many relocating employees and their landlords are unaware this is a legal obligation, not an administrative formality. If the employer is paying rent as part of the relocation package, the employer is the liable party and may face penalties for late stamping. IRAS e-Stamping requires SingPass login — another reason early SingPass registration matters.
non_obvious_action_required: Stamp the tenancy agreement via IRAS e-Stamping within 14 days of signing. Retain the stamped document — it is required if employer claims rent as a business deduction and provides legal protection for both parties. Brief employee on this obligation as part of housing guidance; do not assume their landlord or agent will handle it.
source: IRAS — Stamp Duty for Tenancy Agreements

step: CPF Obligation Assessment — Nil for EP/S Pass/WP Holders
deadline_label: Before first payroll run
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign employees holding an Employment Pass, S Pass, or Work Permit are not eligible for CPF. Employers are not required — and are not permitted — to make CPF contributions for these pass holders.
non_obvious_actual_reality: This is the structural opposite of most European and OECD countries with mandatory pension contributions. No CPF means the employee's take-home pay equals gross salary (minus income tax withholding), but they accrue zero CPF retirement savings in Singapore. Some employers erroneously configure payroll to deduct CPF — this creates an overpayment liability and a CPF Board correction process. Permanent Residents (PRs) DO contribute from Day 1 at different rates from citizens — confusing PR status with EP status is a frequent payroll error.
non_obvious_action_required: Configure payroll system with zero CPF contributions for all EP/S Pass/WP holders before the first pay run. Audit any historical payslips for erroneous CPF deductions. If an employee subsequently obtains PR status mid-year, CPF obligations start with the month of PR grant — set a calendar alert on PR approval date.
source: CPF Board — Who Must Pay CPF Contributions

step: Letter of Consent for Dependant's Pass Holder to Work
applies_to_employee_types: Dependant's Pass holder (spouse of EP holder)
form_name: Letter of Consent (LOC) Application via myMOM
field_label: LOC — Right to Work for DP Holder
deadline_label: Before DP holder commences any employment
responsible_party: Prospective employer of DP holder (applies for LOC)
non_obvious_official_guidance: A Dependant's Pass holder must obtain a Letter of Consent (LOC) from MOM before commencing employment in Singapore. The LOC is employer-specific.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many DP-holding spouses are unaware they cannot work in Singapore simply by virtue of holding a DP. Starting work without an LOC constitutes an immigration offence for both the employee and employer. The LOC is tied to one employer — if the spouse changes jobs, a new LOC must be obtained. Unlike an Employment Pass, the LOC does not confer independent immigration status; the DP (and LOC) are cancelled if the principal EP holder's pass is cancelled.
non_obvious_action_required: Advise EP holder's spouse that they cannot legally work without an LOC. If the spouse has a job offer, the new Singapore employer must apply for the LOC before the start date. Ensure the spouse's employment timeline accounts for LOC processing (typically 3–5 business days). Brief HR on LOC as a standard part of DP onboarding.

step: Foreign Worker Levy Setup — S Pass and WP Employers
form_name: GIRO Direct Debit Authorisation for Levy
deadline_label: Levy billed monthly; GIRO must be set up before first levy cycle
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers of S Pass and Work Permit holders pay a monthly Foreign Worker Levy. S Pass levy: SGD 550 (basic tier, within quota) or SGD 650 (higher tier, above basic quota). WP levy rates vary by sector. Levy is collected via GIRO on the 17th of each month.
non_obvious_actual_reality: EP holders are NOT subject to levy — this is frequently confused in cost modelling when a company transitions an employee from S Pass to EP (levy cost drops to zero). Levy is entirely the employer's cost and cannot be deducted from the employee's salary. Some companies budget total compensation without including levy and face unexpected employer cost overruns. Levy rates increase periodically — budget forecasting must account for scheduled increases.
non_obvious_action_required: Set up GIRO levy payment before the first pass is activated. Include FWL in the employer's total cost of employment model — not just salary and CPF. Track levy tier utilisation against quota ceiling monthly. Subscribe to MOM updates for announced levy rate changes.
source: MOM — Foreign Worker Levy for S Pass

step: IRAS Income Tax — Tax Resident vs Non-Resident Determination
form_name: IRAS myTax Portal — Tax Residency Assessment
field_label: Tax Residency Status: Resident or Non-Resident
deadline_label: Assessed per calendar year; relevant from first Singapore tax filing
non_obvious_official_guidance: A foreigner is a Singapore tax resident if they work in Singapore for ≥183 days in the calendar year. Resident tax rates are progressive: 0% on first SGD 20,000, rising to 24% on income above SGD 1,000,000.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 183-day test is a full calendar year test — not a rolling 12-month window. An employee arriving in August 2025 and working the rest of the year (≈5 months) is a non-resident for all of 2025 even if they remain in Singapore for years. Non-residents pay 15% flat rate OR resident rates — whichever is higher. In most cases, non-resident tax in a partial arrival year is materially higher than the employee expected based on progressive-rate country backgrounds.
non_obvious_action_required: Model year-1 tax liability at non-resident rates for all mid-year arrivals. Discuss with employee whether the employer will provide a tax equalisation or gross-up for Year 1. Consider whether arrival timing can be adjusted (e.g., arriving in early January instead of July) to gain full-year residency sooner. Engage a Singapore tax advisor for any employee earning above SGD 100,000.

step: IRAS Non-Resident Tax — Rate and Director Fee Distinction
field_label: Non-Resident Tax Rate: 15% Employment / 24% Director Fees
deadline_label: Applied at source — employer withholding obligation
non_obvious_official_guidance: Non-resident employees pay 15% flat rate on employment income (or resident rates if higher). Director's fees paid to non-residents are taxed at 24%.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The distinction between employment income and director fees is not merely a label — it is a tax rate trigger. Senior employees who are simultaneously directors of the Singapore entity receive two streams taxed at different non-resident rates. Payroll systems often apply 15% to the entire package. IRAS applies 24% to director fees regardless of employment status — the error surfaces at the tax clearance stage with unexpected underpayment penalties.
non_obvious_action_required: Separate employment income and director fees on payslips and in payroll configuration. Apply 15% withholding to employment income and 24% to director fees for non-resident individuals. Review board appointment letters to confirm which employees hold directorship — this is frequently missed in relocation checklists.

step: Annual Income Tax Filing — Form B1 (Resident) / Form M (Non-Resident)
deadline_label: 15 April (paper); 18 April (e-filing) of the following year
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees whose employer participates in the Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) have employment income auto-populated by IRAS. Filing deadline: 15 April (paper) or 18 April (electronic). IRAS may issue a Notice of Assessment without requiring filing if employer is on AIS.

step: Tax Clearance — IR21 for Departing Non-Citizen Employees
form_name: Form IR21 — Notification of Employee Cessation
deadline_label: At least 1 month before employee cessation / departure from Singapore
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employer must file Form IR21 with IRAS at least 1 month before a non-citizen employee ceases employment, leaves Singapore for more than 3 months, or is sent on overseas posting. IRAS then assesses final tax liability and issues a Tax Clearance Directive.
non_obvious_actual_reality: From the moment IR21 is filed, the employer MUST withhold ALL monies due to the departing employee — salary, accrued leave pay, bonuses, any other compensation — until IRAS issues the Tax Clearance Directive releasing the funds. This mandatory withholding period typically runs 4–6 weeks. Employees (and employers) are routinely caught off-guard: the employee expects final salary on the last working day; the employer is legally prohibited from paying it. Failure to withhold makes the employer personally liable for the employee's outstanding tax.
non_obvious_action_required: Initiate IR21 filing at least 6 weeks before the employee's last day to allow the mandatory withholding period to complete before departure. Notify the employee in writing at the start of the notice period that final pay will be withheld pending IRAS Directive. Coordinate with payroll to freeze salary release date — this requires HR, Finance, and payroll system alignment. File IR21 even if the employee claims to have no Singapore tax liability.
source: IRAS — Tax Clearance for Foreign and SPR Employees (IR21)

step: Employment Pass Renewal — COMPASS Re-Assessment
deadline_label: Apply at least 6 weeks before EP expiry
non_obvious_official_guidance: EP must be renewed before expiry (initially issued for 1–2 years; renewable for up to 3 years). Renewal requires COMPASS re-assessment at current salary benchmarks.
non_obvious_actual_reality: COMPASS applies at renewal using current benchmark data — not the benchmarks that applied at original issue. An employee who passed COMPASS three years ago may fail renewal if their salary has not kept pace with the updated sector percentile benchmarks (which MOM recalibrates annually). Renewal refusals have increased sharply as benchmarks rise. A refused renewal mid-employment triggers an immigration crisis — the employee has no legal basis to continue working.
non_obvious_action_required: Set a calendar reminder 6 months before EP expiry. Re-run the COMPASS self-assessment using current MOM benchmark data. If the employee is near the passing threshold on salary, initiate a compensation review before the renewal application — a salary adjustment is far simpler than managing a renewal refusal. Apply at least 6 weeks before expiry; do not rely on the grace period.

step: Permanent Establishment (PE) Risk Assessment
deadline_label: Before employee commences Singapore-based activities
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under Singapore domestic law and applicable Double Tax Agreements (DTAs), a foreign enterprise with an employee in Singapore who habitually concludes contracts on behalf of the enterprise may create a permanent establishment (PE) subject to Singapore corporate income tax.
non_obvious_actual_reality: PE risk is consistently underestimated in SME relocation planning. Even a single senior employee with authority to negotiate and finalise contracts — without needing home-office approval — can create a Singapore taxable presence for the foreign employer. Once a PE is established, the foreign entity has Singapore corporate tax filing obligations including transfer pricing documentation. IRAS is active in PE audits for cross-border staffing arrangements. This issue is frequently discovered only when IRAS raises an inquiry, by which time multiple years of exposure have accrued.
non_obvious_action_required: Conduct a PE risk review before any senior employee or business developer commences Singapore-based work for a foreign entity. Review the employee's authority scope: procurement authority, contract execution, revenue-generating activities. Engage a Singapore corporate tax advisor — this is definitively consult_professional territory and cannot be self-assessed by HR. Document the review outcome and implement mitigating controls (e.g., countersignature requirements, activity limitations).

step: Social Security — No CPF for Foreigners; No Totalization Agreement with Most Countries
authority: CPF Board / Home Country Pension Authority
field_label: Social Security Obligations: Singapore vs Home Country
deadline_label: Assess before relocation; ongoing for assignment duration
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign employees on EP/S Pass/WP do not contribute to CPF and have no CPF entitlements. Singapore has no bilateral social security totalization agreements with most major sending countries (including India, France, Germany, Philippines, UK, USA).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Unlike the EU/EEA framework (where an A1/E101 certificate eliminates dual social security obligation), Singapore has no equivalent mechanism for most nationalities. The employee may face continued home-country pension obligations (e.g., UK NICs for seconded employees, US FICA for specific assignments) while receiving zero Singapore social security benefit. There is no official certificate of coverage from Singapore CPF that home-country authorities recognise as proof of local social security coverage. This creates potential double contribution obligations for some nationalities that home-country advisors often miss because they assume Singapore has a similar exemption framework.
non_obvious_action_required: Advise employee to independently consult their home-country pension authority (e.g., HMRC for UK nationals, Social Security Administration for US nationals, URSSAF for French nationals) about continued contribution obligations during the Singapore posting. Do not assume home-country exemption applies — the absence of a Singapore totalization agreement means the default in most countries is: contributions continue. Document the advice given and the employee's acknowledgement.
source: CPF Board — CPF for Foreigners; MOM — Work Passes

step: EP/S Pass Cancellation on Employment Cessation
field_label: Work Pass Cancellation within 1 Week of Last Working Day
deadline_label: Within 1 week of last working day
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employer must cancel the employee's work pass within 1 week of the last working day, using the myMOM portal. Dependant's Pass and LTVP linked to the EP/S Pass are automatically cancelled when the main pass is cancelled.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Linked dependant passes are cancelled automatically and simultaneously — the dependant's right to remain in Singapore ends immediately. If a DP-holding spouse has taken a job in Singapore and has an LOC, the LOC is also cancelled when the main EP is cancelled. A departing employee whose family relocation timeline does not align with the EP cancellation date faces a compressed window to make housing and school arrangements.
non_obvious_action_required: Plan pass cancellation date in coordination with the employee's family departure timeline. Do not cancel EP until the family is ready to leave or has secured independent immigration status. If the DP-holding spouse has a job offer and plans to stay, they must secure their own work pass before the principal EP is cancelled — coordinate timelines carefully.

step: Outpatient and Inpatient Medical Insurance — Employer Obligation for WP Holders
deadline_label: In place from day 1 of WP activation
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers of Work Permit holders are legally required to purchase and maintain medical insurance providing at least SGD 15,000 per year of inpatient and day-surgery coverage. This is a condition of the Work Permit.
non_obvious_actual_reality: EP and S Pass employers do NOT have a statutory insurance mandate — only WP employers. However, many HR teams apply the WP insurance standard across all foreign employees without knowing it is not required for EP/S Pass holders (resulting in overspend) or fail to purchase it for WP holders at all (resulting in a pass condition breach). The SGD 15,000 threshold covers basic hospitalisation; it does not cover outpatient, dental, or specialist visits, leaving gaps that employees discover only when they fall ill.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm WP insurance policy is active from the date the Work Permit is activated — not from the first payroll run. Retain policy documents and renewal confirmations in the employee's HR file. Do not confuse WP insurance obligations with general group health insurance. Brief WP holders on what the mandated insurance covers and what out-of-pocket costs they may face.
source: MOM — Medical Insurance for Work Permit Holders
